title: Overview: Li-Fi Light-Based High-Speed Internet
description: Wireless data carried by modulated LED light — gigabit speeds with no radio spectrum needed. The interface is where humans meet the digital world: better displays, audio, and input make technology disappear into everyday life. This database covers all the pieces needed to make it: core components, materials, processes, software, and subsystems, organized on a teaching ladder from Foundations to Advanced. Every record is the full entry with definitions, key facts, and a runnable demo program.

title: Glossary & Quick Reference
description: The working vocabulary of Li-Fi Light-Based High-Speed Internet: Latency, Field of view, Haptics, Eyebox, Foveated rendering, SAR, Pairing, Firmware.
definition: Glossary for Li-Fi Light-Based High-Speed Internet.
key_points: Latency: Delay between action and response — under 20 ms feels instant.
Field of view: How wide the display image appears to the user.
Haptics: Touch feedback: vibration, force, or texture simulation.
Eyebox: The region where the eye sees the full display image.
Foveated rendering: Rendering full detail only where the eye looks.
SAR: Specific absorption rate — regulated RF exposure limit.
Pairing: Connecting a device to a phone or computer wirelessly.
Firmware: Low-level software controlling the device hardware.
